These routes of the platform API come from its [OpenAPI document](../openapi.json); [The REST API as a contract](../rest-api.md) says what Lakana promises about them.

## `POST /api/v1/grants`

Grant a role or an action

From the web interface it needs a passkey touch within the last 15 minutes (403 `StepUpRequired`); a token never does.

Answers 409 when an access file manages the scope; `override_managed` with `override_reason` overrides it (ADMIN on the instance; audited). Answers 409 too, creating nothing, when the principal or group already holds the same role or action on the same object; the message names that grant's id.

Gives a principal or a group a role or a single action on the instance, an environment, a namespace or a table. Needs the `ADMIN` role on the instance. Answers 404 when the principal, group or object does not exist and 422 when the grant is not valid for that object.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `override_managed` | query | no | true or false | Change access in a scope an access file manages anyway, in an emergency. Needs the ADMIN role on the instance and `override_reason`; audited, and shown as drift until the next apply. |
| `override_reason` | query | no | text or null | Why, 10 to 500 characters on one line; with `override_managed=true`. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Request body (application/json, required): `GrantCreate`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `principal` | text or null | no |  |
| `group` | text or null | no |  |
| `role` | `Role` or null | no |  |

| `kind` | `SecurableKind` | yes |  |
| `environment` | text or null | no |  |
| `namespace` | text or null | no |  |
| `table` | text or null | no |  |

Answers:

| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `404` | What the request names does not exist, or the caller may not know that it does. | `ErrorOut` |
| `409` | The request conflicts with the current state; the message says what to change. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

## `GET /api/v1/grants`

List grants

Lists the active grants, newest first. Every filter is optional and narrows the list, except that `principal_name` and `group_name` exclude each other, and so do `role` and `action` (422 when both are given). The object filter matches exactly: `table` with `namespace` and `environment` lists the grants on that table, `namespace` with `environment` those on the namespace, `environment` alone those on the environment. `kind` lists the grants on every object of one kind, in any letter case: `INSTANCE` those on the whole instance, which apply to everything in it; with an object filter it must be that object's kind (422 otherwise). Needs the `ADMIN` role on the instance. Answers 404 when no principal or group has the name given. The cursor of the next page is in the `X-Next-Cursor` response header.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `principal_name` | query | no | text or null | Only grants made to this principal. |
| `group_name` | query | no | text or null | Only grants made to this group. |
| `action` | query | no | text or null | Only grants that give this action (in any letter case): the action, or a role that carries it. |
| `role` | query | no | text or null | Only grants of exactly this role (in any letter case). |
| `environment` | query | no | text or null | The environment of the object filter. |
| `namespace` | query | no | text or null | The dot-joined namespace of the object filter. |
| `table` | query | no | text or null | The table of the object filter. |
| `kind` | query | no | text or null | Only grants on objects of this kind: `INSTANCE`, `ENVIRONMENT`, `NAMESPACE` or `TABLE`. |
| `limit` | query | no | whole number | Most grants returned (1 to 200). |
| `cursor` | query | no | text or null | The `X-Next-Cursor` of the previous page; send the same filters. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Successful Response | list of `GrantOut` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `404` | What the request names does not exist, or the caller may not know that it does. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

## `DELETE /api/v1/grants/{grant_id}`

Revoke a grant

From the web interface it needs a passkey touch within the last 15 minutes (403 `StepUpRequired`); a token never does.

Answers 409 when an access file manages the scope; `override_managed` with `override_reason` overrides it (ADMIN on the instance; audited).

Needs the `ADMIN` role on the instance. Answers 404 when there is no such grant and 409 when revoking it would leave the instance without an active administrator.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `grant_id` | path | yes | text (uuid) | The grant's id. |
| `override_managed` | query | no | true or false | Change access in a scope an access file manages anyway, in an emergency. Needs the ADMIN role on the instance and `override_reason`; audited, and shown as drift until the next apply. |
| `override_reason` | query | no | text or null | Why, 10 to 500 characters on one line; with `override_managed=true`. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `204` | Successful Response | none |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `404` | What the request names does not exist, or the caller may not know that it does. | `ErrorOut` |
| `409` | The request conflicts with the current state; the message says what to change. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |
